precepts.text: When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece. Judah and Ephraim are the bow and the arrow, against the white man. That is war.
precepts.point: When I heard, my belly trembled, my lips quivered, rottenness entered my bones, that I might rest in the day of trouble. The prophets were inside the vision; they could feel the heat and smell the flesh, and Habakkuk did not want to live through it. When he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops, which is why Trump created Space Force and why the UFO files are coming out: the aliens are the angels on the Lord's chariots.
precepts.why:
Habakkuk sees Christ coming: “Thy bow was made quite naked, according to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word.” The oaths of the tribes is the Bible. A bow in hand means you are coming for war, so according to the oaths of Jacob, Christ is coming for war. Zechariah shows what that bow is: “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”.

The Lord bends Judah for himself like a bow and fills the bow with Ephraim: Judah and Ephraim are the bow and the arrow. He raises up the sons of Zion, the rest of the twelve tribes, against the sons of Greece: against the Greeks, the white man. That is war.

That is why this tribulation will not be like any other we have gone through. There will be wars like we have never seen, and in the midst of world war Christ comes: Armageddon. “Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.” Indignation is righteous anger, and he beats the nations in it. The arrows and the glittering spear are the missiles being shot.

And the war is for his people alone: “Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed”. He is only coming to save the twelve tribes of Israel. “Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: that is the white man, and America is the head, discovered “unto the neck” to make sure it is finished. Judah and Ephraim in his hand are how he does it.

precepts.text: When I heard, my belly trembled; when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.
precepts.why:
Christ is returning with clouds, with his chariots and the multitude of angels. Habakkuk saw it: “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself”. Why did he tremble? Because Habakkuk was put in it. He felt it; he saw it.

He trembled “that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.” When Christ comes up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops, the angels.

That is the day of trouble in which the Lord is the mighty protection and strong stay of them that love him. The prophet trembled at what he saw, but those who fear the Lord will rest in that day.

God is “declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done.” Only the God of Israel can do that, and he shows the end to the prophets. Look at the videos of the missiles coming down at night: don't they look like stars falling from heaven? The prophets had never seen a missile, an Iron Dome, a supersonic missile or a nuclear weapon. They described what they saw to the best of their ability, and it is our job to put it together. Put yourself in the prophet's shoes, because you are the prophets; you just don't remember.

Habakkuk describes how it hurts when these missiles hit, because when they hit they bring destruction. You don't want to be around when a missile hits the ground; you don't even want to be ten feet away.

“When I heard, my belly trembled.” That kind of fear is an anxiety sitting inside you, in your chest. He cannot believe what he is watching, but the Lord had to show it to him. “My lips quivered at the voice”: he was shaking, he couldn't even talk straight. “Rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself.” He could not believe the damage this thing was doing, the number of people it killed when it hit.

“That I might rest in the day of trouble.” He is saying, I don't want to be alive to see this. It is so bad I don't want to be around to see it. That is what Psalms 91 means by a thousand falling at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand: he saw the bomb drop and ten thousand people die right there.

That is the end God declared from the beginning, and “My counsel shall stand.” The media say Hamas is finished, Hezbollah has no weapons, Iran is weak; yet Hezbollah fired a hundred missiles into Israel the other day, and Israel cannot destroy Hamas under its nose while Iran is seven times bigger than Israel. We are going with the Bible. If you want the kingdom of heaven, you must accept what comes with it: war, tribulation and death.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
A fire goes before him and burns up his enemies round about: that is Christ coming back to destroy the nations. Habakkuk sees the same coming. “And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power.” His power was hidden in the horns coming out of his hand.

“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet.” That is the fire that goes before him. “He stood, and measured the earth: he beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.” He beholds and drives the nations asunder; the fire round about is his enemies, the nations, being burned up at his return.

When it says displeased against the rivers: “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” So these rivers represent nations. The Lord’s anger against the rivers and his wrath against the sea is his anger against the nations of people.

We’re going to read the whole chapter later, but just for the point: “Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people”. He ain’t coming for the salvation of all races on Earth; he’s coming for the salvation of his people. “Even for salvation with thine anointed”: that’s it right there. “Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: that’s the war; he’s going to kill a whole lot of people.

So when Christ comes: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”. “And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”: we’re going to cry. “And they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” That is God coming from Teman, his glory covering the heavens.

This explains the rivers. “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” So when the Bible talks about water, sometimes it’s making reference to people.

“And he saith unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” That’s the proof that waters are sometimes referenced as people. So when the Lord is displeased against the rivers and his wrath is against the sea, it’s against the nations.
He’s only coming to save the twelve tribes of Israel: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.”

Who is the head of the wicked? “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”. Look up Idumea: pertaining to Edom, the Greek and Roman name for Edom. Christians say Idumea has been destroyed already. Really? Then Christ don’t know what he’s talking about? Idumea is all Caucasians: that’s America, that’s Russia, that’s Germany, France, Britain. That’s Idumea.

So what are you all marrying them for, sisters and brothers? You’re going to get put to death with them; ashes to ashes for you. Christ is coming back to destroy them. This ain’t no racist rant; this is all Bible. Bring us to a court of law: that’s what the Bible says, freedom of speech, we’re going to read what the Bible says.

“And upon the people of my curse”: they are the people of God’s curse, “to judgment.”

The nations coming out as a whirlwind to scatter: “And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another.” This is the proof that when Christ comes back there’s going to be war already on Earth.

“And an innumerable multitude shall be gathered together, as thou sawest them, willing to come, and to overcome him by fighting”: they’re going to try to fight the Son of God. “But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion. And Sion shall come, and shall be shewed to all men”: that’s us, “being prepared and builded, like as thou sawest the hill graven without hands.”

“And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations”: he don’t care about the ICBM missiles and all their various technology. He’s going to rebuke every invention they got; their space force will be crushed and destroyed. “And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented”: they tormented us; Christ is going to torment them. “And he shall destroy them without labour”.

What does it mean, their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly? “Woe unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord”: they have think tanks where they sit around and discuss how to destroy the Israelites. “And their works are in the dark, and they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?” Who’s going to know that we’re sitting here plotting and planning against the twelve tribes of Israel: poisoning food, giving them rap music, destroying their families through welfare and making it sound like we’re trying to help them, guns and drugs and things of that nature.
We read it earlier, but in case y’all forgot: “The wicked plotteth against the just, and gnasheth upon him with his teeth.” That plotting is the devouring of the poor secretly.

This happened during the time of Persia, but it’s relevant for us today; the Bible is very relevant. “But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building”. “And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions”: they get public opinion; they try to get the people in mobs against us. “They hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived”. They did it back then, and they’re doing it now, today.

“And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: bombs dropping, destruction. “And all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree. “The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah”, close to Teman and the Mount of Olives, “and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea.” “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion. And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone.”

“It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever”: that’s America. “But the cormorant and the bittern shall possess it”: those are fowls. “The owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion”: because it’s a land of confusion, “and the stones of emptiness.” “And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons”: a habitation of devils, as in Revelation 18:2 and Isaiah 13:19 and down, “and a court for owls.”

points: Thy bow was made quite naked, according to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word.
The sun and moon stood still in their habitation: at the light of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear.
Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.
Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed; thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked.

points: When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble.

Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls.
Yet I will rejoice in the Lord, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
The Lord God is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds' feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places.

note.label: Habakkuk 3: A Prayer of Habakkuk the Prophet

points: Before we close out: Habakkuk chapter 3. We can’t get out of here without that chapter. “A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet upon Shigionoth. O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid”: I’ve heard what the Bible said, and I was afraid.

“O Lord, revive thy work”: we’re the work. We’re part of that work. Like Ecclesiasticus 36 said, show new signs, make other strange wonders in the earth; a part of that is us waking up. “In the midst of the years”: that’s the 350 years. “In the midst of the years make known”: that’s what you brothers are about, making known God’s works in the street; you sisters, making known God’s works to your children. “In wrath remember mercy”: in your wrath, Lord, remember mercy.
“God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran”: that’s over in the Middle East. “Selah” means it is true. “His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.”

“And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand”: when it says horns, it’s beams of power coming out of his hands. That’s the horns. “And there was the hiding of his power”: he had to hold back some of his power. That’s what the hiding of his power means.

“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet. He stood, and measured the earth”: imagine, the Lord had to measure the earth to see how much power he’s going to use to destroy the nations that come against him. “He beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.”

“I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction”: he said, I saw Ethiopia in affliction. “And the curtains of the land of Midian”: all them in Saudi Arabia, that whole region. He said, I saw them catching hell too.

“Was the Lord displeased against the rivers?” The rivers represent nations: was the Lord displeased against the nations of people? “Was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?” He rides upon his horses and his chariots of salvation.

“Thy bow was made quite naked”: his bow is talking about the Bible. It’s quite obvious God’s coming for war; nowhere does the Bible say he’s coming in peace. “According to the oaths of the tribes”: that’s the proof of what the bow is. “Even thy word”: see that right there, even thy word. That’s what the bow is talking about. “Selah”: it’s true. “Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers.”

“The mountains saw thee, and they trembled”: the mountains are the nations. The nations see Christ, and they’re going to tremble. “The overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice”: the deep of the ocean is going to utter his voice. “And lifted up his hands on high”: tsunamis.
“The sun and moon stood still in their habitation: at the light of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear”: that’s missiles going back and forth, back and forth.
“Thou didst march through the land in indignation”: you march through the land with righteous anger. “Thou didst thresh the heathen in anger”: he’s going to kill the nations in anger.

“Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people”: wait a minute. It didn’t say he came for the salvation of the Jehovah’s Witness or the Pentecostal. It’s thy people. “Even for salvation with thine anointed; thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: he’s going to wound America; that’s the house of the wicked. The head: he’s going to cut their head off. “By discovering the foundation unto the neck”: although the other nations fight America, the Lord said, I got to get in there; I got to finally take them out. “Selah”: it’s true.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages”: that’s Germany, Britain, France and so on. “They came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: they’re coming with their jets, their planes, their missiles to scatter the Son of God. “Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly”: see what God reveals. He’s revealing to us that the nations are plotting against us secretly to destroy each and every one of us.

“Thou didst walk through the sea with thine horses, through the heap of great waters. When I heard, my belly trembled”: when he read the scriptures and saw the vision, his belly trembled. “My lips quivered at the voice”: you know when your bottom lip just trembles because you’re scared as hell? That was Habakkuk. “Rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble”: he said, Lord, when you come back I want to be dead; I want to be resting in heaven when you come back.

“When he cometh up unto the people”: when he comes up to the people, the nations of the world, he will invade them. God is going to invade this earth. So this is the real Space Invaders: when they came up with that game Space Invaders, the Most High already had it in the Bible.

“A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet upon Shigionoth. O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years”. Guess who that work is: us. He’s reviving us. “In wrath remember mercy”.

“God came from Teman”: it’s about Christ. “And the Holy One from mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens”: this is the same thing as in Matthew 24, the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. “And the earth was full of his praise.”

“And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand”: there’s a power emanating from his hands. That’s where you get all these cartoons from; they get it from the word of God, the Bible. There’s going to be power coming out of the Lord’s hand.
“And there was the hiding of his power”: remember, Christ created everything, remember John chapter 1. He’s going to hide some of his power; that’s what he’s saying.
“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet”: destruction comes forth at his feet.

“He stood, and measured the earth”: Christ is going to stand and measure the earth, the circumference of the earth: how much power is required to destroy these nations. “He beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.”
“I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction”: the tents of Cushan is Ethiopia. “And the curtains of the land of Midian did tremble.”

“Was the Lord displeased against the rivers?” When the Bible talks about water, sometimes it’s making reference to people. The rivers are nations: “was thine anger against the rivers?” Nations. “Was thy wrath against the sea”: people, nations. “That thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?”

“Thy bow was made quite naked”: the bow is an instrument of war. The bow it’s talking about, made quite naked, is the word of God, because it’s obvious the Lord is coming back for war. All through the Bible it says God’s coming back for war. Christianity don’t teach that; they say he’s coming back for love and hugs and kisses. That’s not biblical.

“According to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word”: that’s the proof that the bow it’s talking about is the word of God. Believe it or not, this Bible is the oaths of the tribes of Israel. This Bible is not the oath of Esau; it is not the oath of the Philistines or the Jebusites or the Moabites. This Bible is the oath of the twelve tribes of Israel. “Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers.”

“The mountains saw thee, and they trembled: the overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice, and lifted up his hands on high.” Now this is the literal waters, the oceans going up high, like we read earlier about the channels of the waters being seen: that’s what this is talking about.
“The sun and moon stood still in their habitation”: that’s some heavy stuff, like during the time of Joshua. “At the light of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear.”

“Thou didst march through the land in indignation”: righteous anger. “Thou didst thresh the heathen in anger”: the word heathen means nation. He’s going to thresh the heathen, the nations, in anger. Not love: anger.

“Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people”: he’s only coming to save the twelve tribes of Israel; the Lord is coming back to save us. “Even for salvation with thine anointed”: that’s Christ.

“Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: now we know who the head of the wicked is; the head out of the house of the wicked is Idumea. “By discovering the foundation unto the neck”: you cut somebody’s neck and the head comes off. America’s the head of all these nations.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: the nations are going to come out as a whirlwind to try to scatter the Son of God and his angels.
“Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly”: the rejoicing of the nations was as to devour the poor secretly.

Remember he said, is wisdom no more in Teman: Dedan is going to flee when Christ lands on the Mount of Olives and cleaves the mountain in four places. “O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years”: the Lord’s work. “In the midst of the years make known”: make things known to us. Making known goes back to turning the heart of the fathers to the children and the children to the fathers. “In wrath remember mercy.”

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “God came from Teman”: who came from Teman? God. Teman goes to the Mount of Olives; when he landed on the Mount of Olives. “And the Holy One from mount Paran”: in that same area. “His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.”

Put the maps up and you see the Mount of Olives is right there, close to Edom. They’re next door; he’s going there for a reason. Lebanon is above Jerusalem and Teman is right under it, so it’s next door; maybe about 60 miles off, very close. Teman is there, Edom right there, Dedan is right in that area, and Bozrah is all that area. Keep that in mind.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “And his brightness was as the light”: he had power all around his body, like them chariots, radiant energy. “He had horns coming out of his hand”: he had beams of light in his hand like a superhero. “And there was the hiding of his power”: he had to hold back, because he would destroy every damn thing.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet”: so when he landed he caused the earthquake, and everything melted under his feet.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “Was the Lord displeased against the rivers?” Yes, he was. “Was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea”: the nations. “That thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?” He is going to ride upon a chariot. He’s going to come with his Chariot; he’s going to bring his car with him.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers. The mountains saw thee, and they trembled”: they split in four. “The overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice, and lifted up his hands on high.”

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.”

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed”, against “the head out of the house of the wicked”: the house of the thief. “By discovering the foundation unto the neck”: he cut the entire head off. Christ finishes Esau off himself.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “They came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: they ain’t going to beat him. “Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly”: they tried to destroy us secretly.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble”: he prayed he was dead during that time. I want to see that in real life. “When he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops”: he will come with his saints, as in Zechariah 14.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: There are secret plots at work. Yes, there are conspiracies, and yes, the Bible reveals there are conspiracies going on against the twelve tribes of Israel. ‘Oh, you’re crazy, that thing with the food, you guys are insane, they can’t weaponize food.’ Negro please, stop.
“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages”: when the Lord comes back he is going to strike through with his staves the head of the white man’s villages, his countries.
“They came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: the nations are going to come against Christ to try to scatter him and destroy him.

“Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” See what the nations wanted to do: destroy us secretly. Who’s going to stand up on the media and say, hey, yeah, we want to kill all the twelve tribes? They’re not going to do that. Their rejoicing was to destroy the poor secretly. Let’s get our minds right.
